title: Will Benjamin Netanyahu cease to be Prime Minister of Israel during 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, at any point before January 1, 2027, Benjamin Netanyahu ceases to be Prime Minister of Israel.

This includes Netanyahu getting suspended, an acting Prime Minister being appointed, or any other temporary circumstance that removes his power, if it lasts for at least 14 consecutive days entirely within 2026.
background:
[Benjamin Netanyahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu) is the Prime Minister of Israel as of December 2025, having held the office from 1996 to 1999, from 2009 to 2021 and from 2022 to 2025. Netanyahu is the longest-tenured prime minister in the country's history, having led the government for a total of over 18 years.

During Netanyahu's leadership, he has experienced substantial challenges including charges of [bribery and fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_of_Benjamin_Netanyahu), [arrest warrants from the ICC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court_arrest_warrants_for_Israeli_leaders) due to Israel's actions in Gaza, and mixed support from the Israeli public.

With an [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Israeli_legislative_election) required before October 27, 2026, Netanyahu's government faces differing opinion polls, though some pollsters have been implicated in breach of trust and are known to be affiliated with Netanyahu.

comments.text:
**0.18.** CP is too high.

* **Netanyahu is already the caretaker PM.** The Knesset **dissolved on 2026‑07‑17** and an election is **fixed for 2026‑10‑27**. Israeli law says a caretaker/transitional PM *keeps the office and title* until a successor government is sworn in - so the dissolution and election do **not** by themselves resolve YES.
* **The only live YES route is tightly time‑boxed.** A *different* PM must be sworn in during the 65‑day Oct 27 → Dec 31 window. A non‑Netanyahu government has never formed faster than **82 days**; the opposition is fragmented with no agreed PM. Electoral‑route YES: 0.12-0.15. Legal removal (needs a final conviction, verdict 2027+), resignation (refused, caretaker‑gated), and forced ≥14‑day incapacity are all \~0; only \~1.5–2% mortality is an independent floor.

comments.author: Sitric
comments.text:
Benjamin Netanyahu remaining Prime Minister for all of 2026 looks slightly more likely than not. I’d put the probability that he ceases to be the prime minister at about 25–35%. I've chosen 32%. I might push that up as per what happens with how the Iranians respond to the US/Israel attack on Iran. I don't foresee the Iranians holding back in their retaliation this time as they did last time. If/when the Golden dome runs out of interceptor missiles and the Iranian missiles begin hitting targets, it may create even more political pressure on Netanyahu. But as of right now, I'm going 32%.

## What I considered

* The next regular Knesset election is scheduled for 27 October 2026, so by default he stays in office through most of 2026 unless early elections, a no‑confidence vote, or a budget crisis bring the government down earlier.
* Analyses of the upcoming 2026 election describe it as highly contentious but still note Netanyahu and his Likud party as leading contenders and likely to remain the focal candidate for the right‑wing and religious parties, which suggests continuing coalition support going into the election window.
* His coalition depends on tight bloc with parties like Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power), and the ultra-Orthodox Shas and UTJ. Without those groups he is not near the 61 seats. A single one of those parties dropping out or failing the threshold would destroy his majority. The ultra-Orthodox have already shown willingness to quit or threaten to do so if they don't get their demands (e.g draft law). That would immediately deprive him of a majority and force consideration of early elections or replacement government. The far-rights demands on invasion of Gaza, expansion of settlements in the Palestinian West Bank, changes to law to execute Palestinian (including arab Israeli citizens) prisoners but exclude Jewish convicts, etc are also a large pressure on him.
* His position is under unusually heavy strain: ongoing ICC arrest warrants, domestic polarization after the Gaza war, and coalition instability (loss of majority and risk of early elections if the budget fails or no‑confidence passes) materially raise the chance of him being forced out or choosing to step aside before year‑end 2026.

Putting that together: structural factors (incumbency, scheduled election date, coalition arithmetic) still slightly favor him remaining in office through 2026, but legal, political, and other pressures are strong enough that a forced or negotiated exit during 2026 is a possibility.
